Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

We open this session with what we concluded in the explanation of the last part of Surah an-Naba, where we reached Surah at-Takathur.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase diverts you, until you visit the graves.﴾ [at-Takathur 1, 2] This sentence is a declarative statement in which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informs His servants, addressing them, saying: ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase diverts you﴾. The meaning of ﴿diverts you﴾ is: it occupies you, until you become heedless of what is more important than remembering Allah, Most High, and carrying out His obedience. The address here is to the entire Ummah, except that it is restricted to those whom the matters of the Hereafter have occupied away from the matters of this world, and they are few. We say they are few because it is established in the two Sahihs that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says on the Day of Resurrection: 'O Adam!' He says: 'At Your service, and at Your pleasure.' He says: 'Bring out from your offspring a contingent for the Fire.' He says: 'And what is the contingent for the Fire?' He says: 'Out of every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine.'"[[Related by al-Bukhari (4741), and the wording is his, and Muslim (222/379), from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says on the Day of Resurrection: O Adam. He says: At Your service, our Lord, and at Your pleasure. It will be called out with a voice: Indeed Allah commands you to bring out from your offspring a contingent for the Fire. He says: O Lord, and what is the contingent for the Fire? He says: Out of every thousand—I think he said—nine hundred and ninety-nine..." The hadith.]] One is in Paradise and the rest are in the Fire, and this is a huge number. If there were none of the children of Adam except one out of a thousand who are the people of Paradise, and the rest are the people of the Fire, then the generality of address in a verse like this remains on its basis, because one out of a thousand is nothing in comparison to them.

As for His saying: ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase﴾, it includes rivalry in wealth, rivalry in tribe, rivalry in rank, rivalry in knowledge, and everything in which boasting may occur. This is shown by the saying of the owner of the garden to his companion: ﴿I am more than you in wealth and mightier in men﴾ [al-Kahf 34]. A person may compete in his wealth, seeking to have more wealth than the other and wider trade. A person may compete in his tribe, saying: We are more numerous than them, as the poet said:

You are not among the most numerous of them in pebbles,
but honour belongs to the one who has more.

(More numerous of them in pebbles) because in former times they used to count things by pebbles. For example: if these people have ten thousand pebbles and the others have eight thousand, the first becomes what? More numerous and more honoured. So the poet says:

You are not among the most numerous of them in pebbles,
but honour belongs to the one who has more.

Likewise, a person may compete in knowledge, and you find him boasting over others with knowledge. But if it is knowledge of the Sharia, it is good; and if it is knowledge other than the Sharia, it is either permissible or forbidden. The point is that among the things in which rivalry occurs is knowledge, and this is what prevails among the children of Adam: rivalry. They compete in these matters, diverted from what they were created for, namely the worship of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

As for His saying: ﴿until you visit the graves﴾, it means: until you visit the graves, i.e., until you die. A person is inclined to rivalry until he dies. Indeed, the more old age increases in him, the more hope increases in him: he grows old in years and young in hope. Thus a man who is ninety years old, for example, you find in him more hopes and longer hope than a young man who is fifteen. This is the meaning of the noble verse; that is, you were distracted by rivalry from the Hereafter until you died.

It has been said that the meaning of ﴿until you visit the graves﴾ is: until you come to compete by the dead just as you compete by the living, so a person comes and says: My tribe is more numerous than your tribe, and if you wish, go to the graves, count the graves of us and count the graves of you, which of us is more? But this is a weak opinion, far from the context of the verse, and the first meaning is the correct one, namely that you compete until you die.

Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, used His saying: ﴿until you visit the graves﴾ as evidence that the visitor must return to his homeland, and that graves are not a place of permanent residence. It is also mentioned that some Bedouins heard a reciter recite: ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase diverts you, until you visit the graves﴾, and he said: "By Allah, we will surely be resurrected!" Why? Because the visitor, as is well known, visits and returns. So he said: "By Allah, we will surely be resurrected." And this is the truth. By this we know that what some people now say in newspapers and elsewhere, that when a man dies, "he has moved to his final abode," is false and a lie; for the grave is not the final abode. Rather, if a person believed the meaning of this expression, he would become what? A disbeliever in the Resurrection, and disbelief in the Resurrection is apostasy from Islam. But many people take words at face value and do not know their meaning, and perhaps this is inherited from the atheists who do not affirm resurrection after death.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿No! You will soon know.﴾ ﴿Again, no! You will soon know.﴾ [At-Takathur 3–4] It has been said that ﴿Kalla﴾ means restraint (ar-radʿ), i.e., "Desist from this rivalry in accumulation." It has also been said that it means "truly" (ḥaqqan).

The meaning of ﴿You will soon know﴾ is: you will soon know the outcome of your affair when you return to the Hereafter, and that this accumulation will not benefit you. It has come in a hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ), as narrated by Muslim[[Recorded by Muslim (2958/3) from the hadith of ʿAbdullah ibn ash-Shikhkhir, may Allah be pleased with him, and its wording is: "The son of Adam says: 'My wealth, my wealth.' He said: 'And do you have of your wealth, O son of Adam, anything except what you have eaten and consumed, or worn and worn out, or given in charity and sent ahead?'"]] that "the servant says: 'My wealth, my wealth,'" meaning he boasts of it, "and you have of your wealth only what you have eaten and consumed, or worn and worn out, or given in charity and sent forth; and the rest you leave for others." This is the truth. Now, our wealth that is in our hands is either something we eat, and it perishes; or something we wear, and then what? It wears out; or something we give in charity, and we send it forward, and it will be before us on the Day of Resurrection; or we leave it for others. The wealth in our hands cannot escape this fourfold division.

﴿No! You will soon know﴾ means: you will soon know the outcome of your affair through the accumulation that has distracted you from the Hereafter.

﴿Again, no! You will soon know﴾: this sentence is an emphasis of the restraint a second time.

Then He said: ﴿Nay, if you knew with the knowledge of certainty﴾ [At-Takathur 5]. Meaning: Truly, if you knew with the knowledge of certainty, you would know that you are in error. But you do not know with the knowledge of certainty, because you are heedless and distracted in this worldly life. Had you known with the knowledge of certainty, you would have known that you are in error and in a great mistake.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire (6). Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾ [At-Takathur 6-7]. ﴿You will surely see﴾: this sentence is independent and is not the answer to (law, "if"). For this reason the reader must pause at His saying: ﴿Nay, if you knew with the knowledge of certainty﴾. We often hear some imams who have knowledge join it and say: ﴿Nay, if you knew with the knowledge of certainty (5) you will surely see the Hellfire﴾. This joining is either heedlessness and forgetfulness on their part, or they have not contemplated the verse as they should. Otherwise, had they contemplated it as it deserves, they would have found that joining corrupts the meaning. For when he says: ﴿Nay, if you knew with the knowledge of certainty (5) you will surely see the Hellfire﴾, the seeing of the Hellfire becomes conditional upon what? Upon their knowledge. This is not correct. Therefore it is necessary to be attentive and to alert others to this. If you hear anyone reading: ﴿Nay, if you knew with the knowledge of certainty (5) you will surely see the Hellfire﴾, alert him; say: "O brother, your joining gives the impression of corrupted meaning, so stop." First, because it is the end of a verse, and it is prescribed that a person pause at the end of every verse. Second, because joining corrupts the meaning.

﴿Nay, if you knew with the knowledge of certainty (5) you will surely see the Hellfire﴾. Therefore ﴿you will surely see the Hellfire﴾ is a resumed sentence with no connection to what precedes it. It is a oath-sentence containing an implied oath, and the estimate is: "By Allah, you will surely see the Hellfire." For this reason, the grammarians say in its parsing: the lam is a preparatory lam for the oath (lam al-muwatta'ah), and the clause "(tarawunna)" is the answer to the oath, and the oath is elided, the estimate being: "By Allah, you will surely see the Hellfire." And ﴿al-Jahim﴾ is one of the names of the Fire.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 102, verse 7:

﴿Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty.﴾ [At-Takathur: 7] This is an emphasis on seeing it. And when will it be seen? It will be seen on the Day of Resurrection. It will be brought forth, dragged by seventy thousand ropes (zimam), with each rope being pulled by seventy thousand angels.[[Muslim (2842/29) narrated from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "On that Day Hell will be brought forth, having seventy thousand ropes, with each rope held by seventy thousand angels dragging it."]] So consider what this abode is like, may Allah protect us. It is a vast and immense abode, for it has seventy thousand ropes, each rope pulled by seventy thousand angels, and the angels are mighty and severe. It is a great fire, may Allah protect us and you from it.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 102, verse 8:

﴿You shall surely see the Hellfire. Then you shall surely see it with the certainty of sight. Then you shall surely be questioned that Day about the bliss.﴾ [At-Takathur: 6–8] Meaning: then, at that time, in that great standing, you will be questioned about the bliss.

The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, differed concerning His saying: ﴿Then you shall surely be questioned that Day about the bliss.﴾ Is the intended meaning the disbeliever alone, or both the believer and the disbeliever? The correct view is that the intended meaning is both the believer and the disbeliever: each will be questioned about the bliss. However, the disbeliever will be questioned with a questioning of rebuke and reproach, while the believer will be questioned with a questioning of reminder. The evidence that it is general is what happened in the story of the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Bakr and 'Umar, "when they went out one day because of hunger, and they went to the orchard of a man called Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan, and asked permission to enter. The Prophet ﷺ said, 'As-salamu 'alaykum,' and his wife was behind the door and did not return the greeting. He said, 'As-salamu 'alaykum,' and she did not return it. He said, 'As-salamu 'alaykum,' and she did not return it. So the Prophet ﷺ and his companions turned away," because a person who asks permission three times and is not admitted returns. "She caught up with them and said: 'I heard your greeting, but I wanted to increase in good.'" Meaning: the Messenger was invoking peace upon them, and she wished for the Messenger's prayer for them, peace and blessings be upon him, to be repeated. "So they returned and asked about her husband, and she said: 'He has gone to fetch sweet water,' that is, to bring good, pleasant water. They sat down, then the man came, and he was overjoyed to see them and said: 'There is no one more generous in hospitality than me today.' Then he cut for them a bunch of dates from a palm and brought it and placed it before them. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Why did you not pick them?' ('Janeyta' means 'kharafta,' that is, you picked them, and you know that kharaf is when a person takes only the ripe dates.) He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I wanted there to be before you the unripe, the half-ripe and the ripe dates.' Because 'idhq' includes this and that, it includes all three. So they ate, then they asked for water and drank. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Good water, good food, and good shade, you will surely be questioned about them that Day concerning the bliss.'"[[Abu Ya'la related (250) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out at midday and found Abu Bakr in the mosque, and said: "What brought you out at this hour?" He said: "What brought you out has brought me out, O Messenger of Allah." 'Umar ibn al-Khattab came and he said: "O Ibn al-Khattab, what brought you out?" He said: "What brought you out, O Messenger of Allah, has brought me out." 'Umar sat, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and spoke to them both, then said: "Do you have any strength to set out to this palm grove and obtain food, drink and shade?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Go with us to the house of Ibn al-Tayyihan, Abu al-Haytham al-Ansari." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went ahead of us, greeted and asked permission three times, while Umm al-Haytham was behind the door hearing the speech and wishing that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would increase it for her. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wanted to leave, Umm al-Haytham came out running after them and said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I heard your greeting, but I wanted you to increase your peace upon us." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said good things to her and said: "Where is Abu al-Haytham? I do not see him." She said: "He is nearby, he has gone to fetch sweet water for us. Enter, for he will come at once, God willing." She spread a rug for them under a tree, and Abu al-Haytham came, rejoiced at them, his eye was delighted by them, and he climbed a palm tree and cut a bunch for them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Enough, O Abu al-Haytham." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, you eat of its unripe dates, its ripe dates and its half-ripe dates." Then he brought them water and they drank over it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This is from the bliss about which you will be questioned..." the hadith. In the hadith of Abu Hurayrah in al-Tirmidhi (2369): The Prophet ﷺ said: "Why did you not select for us from its ripe dates?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I wanted you to choose, or he said: choose from its ripe and unripe dates." They ate and drank from that water..." the hadith.]], and this is evidence that both the believer and the disbeliever will be questioned, but the questioning differs. The believer's questioning is a reminder of the blessing of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, upon him, so that he rejoices and knows that the One who bestowed His blessings upon him in this world will bestow His blessings upon him in the Hereafter; that is, if He was generous with His blessing to him in this world, He will be generous to him with His blessing in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, it is a questioning of rebuke and regret.

We ask Allah, the Exalted, to employ us and you in His obedience, and to make what He has provided us a help in obeying Him. Indeed, He is capable of all things.
